requirement: SCE-MI message channels shall be optimized for implementing abstraction bridges between a software subsystem and a hardware subsystem.

targets.possible_definition: An interface layer connecting and translating communication between hardware and software subsystems.
Standard Co-Emulation Modeling Interface; infrastructure connecting hardware and software execution environments.
A high-performance communication conduit optimized for software-hardware interaction.

requirement: Transactor names shall conform to the syntax of the HDL language that the bridge netlist is expressed in.

targets.possible_definition: A high-level interface component converting abstract software calls into hardware signals.
Hardware Description Language; code syntax used to express netlists and hardware models.
The lower-level structural circuit representation of an abstraction bridge.

requirement: The SCE-MI infrastructure shall always implicitly create a controlled clock with a 1/1 ratio, which is the highest frequency controlled clock in the system

targets.possible_definition: The hardware-software co-emulation infrastructure environment.
A system clock whose execution can be started or stopped by transactor instruction.

requirement: Any transactor shall be able to instruct the SCE-MI infrastructure to stop the controlled clock and thus cause controlled time to freeze.

targets.possible_definition: A bridge component with the authority to pause time execution in the hardware model.
The core co-emulation infrastructure managing simulation timing and hardware clocks.
A stoppable clock signal driving the emulation hardware.
Simulated time progress governed directly by controlled clock cycles.

requirement: The SCE-MI infrastructure shall feature cycle stamping.

targets.possible_definition: The underlying emulation architecture managing signal timing.
A timing mechanism that attaches exact clock-cycle timestamps to message transactions.

requirement: Before messages can be transported over a SCE-MI message channel, their content must be serialized into a large bit vector by the DUT proxy model.

targets.possible_definition: The co-emulation framework defining communication structures.
The bus transport mechanism over which bit vectors travel.
A software modeling adapter that serializes message data for transmission to the DUT.
High-level data structures serialized into bit vectors for channel transmission.

requirement: The DUT shall always be clocked by one or more controlled clocks that are controlled by one or more transactors.

targets.possible_definition: Device Under Test; the primary hardware design or model being emulated.
Clock signals governing the DUT that can be frozen by controlling transactors.
Interface controllers tasked with driving controlled clocks on the DUT.

requirement: The users shall be able to specify that they only care about posedges of the cclock and do not care where the negedge falls.

targets.possible_definition: The rising edge transition (from low to high) of the controlled clock.
The falling edge transition (from high to low) of the controlled clock.
The controlled clock signal whose edge transitions dictate hardware state evaluation.

requirement: Controlled clocks shall have a 1/1 ratio which, when enabled, is the same frequency as the uncontrolled clocks

targets.possible_definition: Emulation clocks that run matching the frequency of uncontrolled clocks when active.
Free-running system clock signals operating at continuous baseline frequencies.

requirement: For output messages, the transactor shall accept the clocked events originating from the DUT hardware model, and assemble them into serialized bit streams.

targets.possible_definition: Output data streams assembled from clocked hardware events.
A hardware-software translator that converts raw DUT clock events into serialized messages.
Signal state changes output by the DUT hardware model on clock cycles.
Device Under Test; the target hardware implementation emitting output events.
The underlying target hardware representation executing inside the emulator.
